reuse.why: Builds on the tree's single weekend rule (applyWeekendRule/applyWeekendRuleToDay), recurConfigToRSchedule and RSchedule, extending them for holidays rather than writing new date logic.

duplication.why: The daily 'skip instead of move' decision (skipsWeekendOccurrences + isNonWorkingDay filter, and a 7+holidays look-ahead) is re-assembled at four places: getNextDate, getUpcomingDates, getDatesInRange and the schedule-template loop, and getDatesInRange repeats the getUpcomingDates pipeline.

placement.why: The rule pieces live in shared/schedules.ts and the new handler sits next to schedule/get-upcoming-dates in server/schedules/app.ts, matching the tree's layering.

scope.why: Changes follow the four steps (plus release notes and the parseRecurDate data needed for frequency/holidays) without unrelated edits.

maintainability.why: Holidays are cleanly threaded through one weekend rule, but whether an occurrence is skipped or moved is decided separately at each caller with ad-hoc look-ahead bounds, so a future rule change must touch four sites.

bypasses_abstraction.where: The skip-vs-move decision is not part of applyWeekendRule; getUpcomingDates, getDatesInRange (server/schedules/app.ts), getNextDate (shared/schedules.ts) and createScheduleList (server/budget/schedule-template.ts) each filter non-working days themselves around it.

disguised_duplication.where: The same skip filter appears as pickDate in getNextDate, a .filter in getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange, and an if-guard plus resolveDate closure in schedule-template, reshaped at each site rather than shared.

abstraction_drift.where: holidays parameter added to applyWeekendRule, applyWeekendRuleToDay and getDateWithSkippedWeekend; getNextDate gains a daily-skip branch; getNextDate, getUpcomingDates, getDatesInRange and schedule-template's createScheduleList decide daily skipping outside the weekend rule.
